paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : GPQA confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for three different measures—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—across a range of initial confidence values from 0.91 to 0.99. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is scaled linearly with values marked at intervals of 0.01, ranging from 0.91 to 0.99. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also linear, with values ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. The blue line with square markers, representing Final Accuracy, remains consistently high, fluctuating slightly around 0.9 and peaking at approximately 1.0 at an initial confidence of 0.93. The green line with circular markers, representing Initial Accuracy, shows a general upward trend, starting at approximately 0.35 at 0.91 and rising to about 0.85 at 0.99. The orange line with diamond markers, representing Δ Accuracy, exhibits a more volatile pattern, beginning at around 0.55, peaking at 0.68 at 0.92, and then declining to a low of approximately 0.1 at 0.98 before rising slightly to 0.17 at 0.99. Error bars are present for all data points, indicating variability in the measurements.
